title: From First Principles to Modern LLMs
description: Unbroken chain of derivation: sets → analysis → linear algebra → probability → information theory → optimization → neural networks → attention → transformer → pre-training → SFT → RLHF/DPO.

chapters.title: Sets, functions, logic, proofs
Numbers, sequences, limits, completeness
Continuity, univariate differentiation, chain rule
Multivariate calculus: partials, gradients, Jacobians
Linear algebra I: vector spaces, basis, linear maps
Linear algebra II: inner products, norms, eigenvalues, SVD
Convexity and optimization; gradient descent convergence
Probability foundations: sample spaces, sigma-algebras, Kolmogorov axioms
Random variables, distributions, CDF/PMF/PDF
Expectation, variance, covariance; Jensen's inequality
Information theory: self-information, entropy, cross-entropy, KL
Statistical inference: likelihood, MLE, ERM, bias-variance
SGD: stochastic-approximation theorem; mini-batching; convergence sketch
Momentum, RMSProp, AdamW: derivation and bias-correction proof
MLPs as compositional functions; universal approximation
Activation functions: ReLU/GELU/softmax with derivatives
Loss functions: MSE, cross-entropy; gradients from first principles
Backpropagation: chain rule applied; reverse-mode AD as a graph algorithm
Embeddings: token to vector; lookup as a linear map; weight tying
RNN intuition; vanishing-gradient proof; why we need attention
Scaled dot-product attention: derivation, softmax-temperature analysis
Multi-head attention: parallel heads as concat-then-project; complexity
Transformer block: residual + LayerNorm/RMSNorm + FFN + attention; gradient-flow argument
Positional encoding: sinusoidal derivation, RoPE construction
Causal masking; next-token prediction loss as MLE on the empirical distribution
Tokenization: BPE algorithm; greedy merge correctness
Pre-training pipeline: AdamW + warmup + cosine decay + gradient clipping; tiny-GPT training run
SFT, RLHF (PPO/GRPO), and DPO; train + post-train a tiny GPT
